title: Service reliability orientation lab and 90-day experiments
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, practical plan for running a Service Reliability Orientation Lab followed by a rolling set of 90-day reliability experiments across product, serving-runtime, infra, and SRE. The goal is to accelerate SLO adoption, surface low-effort/high-impact fixes, and build shared expectations across teams in a way that scales across 10+ services. This doc is intentionally pragmatic: half-day workshops, small experiment bets, clear success criteria, and a simple communication cadence.

Context and problem statement:
- We have many teams consuming Redwood Inference runtime features (hosting, dedicated, private) with uneven SLO instrumentation and differing operational playbooks.
- Incident handoffs and post-incident actions are inconsistent; some services have mature error budgets, others lack alerts aligned to user-visible latency/reliability.
- Previous SLO initiatives produced long roadmaps but limited operational change. This orientation lab + 90-day experiment structure aims for measurable changes in the next quarter.

Who should read this:
- Service owners, platform engineers, product managers, SREs, on-call engineers, solutions engineers with customer-facing SLAs.

High-level approach:
1) Orientation Lab (week 0): a lightweight, cross-functional half-day working session per service group to align on concepts, pick an SLO target, and define 1–2 experiment bets to run for 90 days.
2) Rolling 90-day experiments: maintain a 90-day timeline per service with clear metrics, weekly syncs, and a sprint-style backlog of work items (triage -> implement -> measure).
3) Graduation/Handoff: after 90 days the experiment is either (a) promoted into standard operating procedure with runbooks and dashboards, (b) iterated with new hypotheses for another 90 days, or (c) shelved with lessons captured.

Orientation Lab (detailed):
- Participants: service PM or TL, 1 SRE, 1 runtime engineer (serving/runtime), 1 infra rep (if relevant), product analytics owner, customer success rep (optional).
- Pre-work (2 days before lab): collect request/latency/availability graphs for last 30 days, current alert definitions, existing SLIs/SLOs (if any), recent P0/P1 incident summaries. Upload to shared folder.
- Agenda (3.5 hours):
  - 0:00–0:20 — Framing: short review of cause/effect for reliability and business outcomes. State desired customer experience in one sentence.
  - 0:20–0:50 — Current state review: walk the metrics pack. Identify the top 2 signals that map directly to customer experience (eg 99th percentile p95/p99 latency, successful completion rate, model failure rate).
  - 0:50–1:20 — SLI/SLO selection exercise: pick 1 primary SLO and 1 secondary SLI. Use an SLO template (see below).
  - 1:20–2:10 — Hypothesis generation: brainstorm small experiments (batching config change, KV cache tweak, alert threshold change, routing policy change, canary rollout plan) and estimate order-of-magnitude effort and impact. Capture 3 candidate bets.
  - 2:10–2:40 — Decide on 1 primary experiment and 1 fallback. Assign owners and define weekly checkpoints.
  - 2:40–3:15 — Communications + playbook: what to post to #reliability-updates, who owns oncall escalations, shared dashboard links, and where to record runbook steps.
  - 3:15–3:30 — Quick retro: what concerns or blockers do participants foresee?

SLO template (fill in during lab):
- Service name: (string)
- Customer-visible objective (one sentence): e.g., "Customer requests should succeed and respond within X ms for Y% of requests in a sliding 28-day window."
- SLI definition (primary): metric name and measurement window (e.g., request_success_rate over 28d, p99_inference_latency measured on tail requests).
- SLO target: e.g., 99.5% success or p99 < 1.2s for production traffic.
- Error budget policy: monthly burn threshold, escalation steps when burn > 20% in a 7-day window.
- Measurement owner: person/team responsible for dashboards and alerts.
- Runbook location: Google Drive / Confluence link.

90-day experiment structure:
- Sprint cadence: weekly async updates (status card), biweekly 30-min alignment call with SRE program lead.
- Backlog items: prioritized and small (<5 engineer-days) where possible. Use an experiment board with states: hypothesis -> in-progress -> gated test -> measure -> decision.
- Measurement plan: baseline window (14 days before changes), signal windows (day 7, day 30, day 60, day 90). Define primary metric and 2 secondary safety metrics (error rate, CPU/GPU utilization, cost delta).
- Success criteria: explicit pass/fail conditions. Examples: reduce p99 latency by >=15% with <=5% cost increase AND maintain success rate above 99.0%.
- Safety gates: rollback triggers (increase in error rate >= 1.5x baseline, sustained GPU saturations > 75% for 10 minutes).

Sample experiment bets (examples to seed labs):
- Prefix KV caching: enable prefix cache for specific high-frequency prompts; measure latency and token cost.
- Dynamic batching threshold: lower batching max latency threshold for low-latency endpoints during peak hours.
- Quantization profile A/B: test int8 quantized runtime variant on non-critical traffic to measure cost reduction vs quality.
- Regional routing tweak: shift 10% of traffic to lower-latency region for a canary window to observe network and cold-start effects.
- Alert tuning: move from static 95th-percentile alert to adaptive baseline alert to reduce noise and increase signal-to-noise for true regressions.

Roles and responsibilities:
- Service owner (PM/TL): accountable for business objective and approving SLO target.
- SRE lead (experiment owner): runs the orientation lab, coordinates experiment backlog, monitors metrics and runs weekly sync.
- Runtime engineer: implements serving/runtime configuration changes and validates behavior.
- Infra rep: ensures node sizing, scaling and quotas are sufficient for experiment.
- Observability/analytics: validates dashboards, helps define measurement windows and computes error budget burn.

Communication plan:
- Weekly status card (one paragraph) posted to #reliability-updates with link to dashboard.
- Biweekly show-and-tell in Reliability Office Hours (15–20m demonstration of progress).
- All retrospective notes and final decision captured in Confluence page referenced by linked_artifacts.

Risk register (top 5 potential blockers):
- Insufficient observability (missing telemetry for chosen SLI) -> Mitigation: instrument synthetic test and add tracing events in first 2 weeks.
- Resource limits in dedicated pools -> Mitigation: reserve small canary pool or coordinate with dedicated infra for temporary quota.
- Customer-facing regressions after change -> Mitigation: strict canary policy and rollback runbook.
- Cross-team bandwidth -> Mitigation: cap experiment to 5 engineer-days per sprint and prioritize minimal-scope changes.
- Measurement noise -> Mitigation: require >=2 independent signals (latency + success rate) before changing SLOs.

Operational artifacts to deliver by day 90:
- Final SLO definition and dashboard link.
- A concise runbook for oncall and playbook for mitigation (max 2 pages).
- Experiment report: hypothesis, actions, measurements, decision, next steps.
- If promoted: PRs for infra/runtime defaults and a rollout checklist.

How to run multiple services in parallel:
- Stagger lab start weeks across service cohorts so program team can support 3 concurrent 90-day experiments comfortably.
- Reuse experiment blueprints (e.g., cache toggle checklist, quantization test recipe) so service-specific effort is reduced.
- Maintain a lightweight shared tracker with columns: service, start_date, SLO chosen, experiment owner, status, decision_date.

Metrics we will track at program level:
- Number of services with canonical SLOs (target + baseline) per quarter.
- % of experiments promoted to SOPs after 90 days.
- Median time from lab to first measurable improvement in SLI (goal: <=30 days).
- Reduction in alert fatigue (alerts per oncall shift, target: -20% in three months for participating teams).

Next steps (owner assignments):
- Aisha: schedule first two orientation labs (service cohort A) and prepare lab template (due 2026-02-17).
- Liam: build experiment board template and deck for labs (due 2026-02-15).
- Rosa: validate observability pre-check script and identify synthetic tests (due 2026-02-16).
- Evan: reserve canary infra pools and list quota request process (due 2026-02-18).

Notes and open questions:
- Should we default SLO measurement window to 28-day rolling by policy or leave per-service choice? (Proposed: default 28d with clear opt-out reasons.)
- What’s the expected approval flow for promoting an experiment into an org-level default? (Proposed: service owner + SRE program lead + infra leads sign-off.)
- Budget for extra infra during experiments (small): should this be a centralized fund or charged to team? (Open; discuss with finance.)

Appendix: Quick checklists
- Lab pre-checks: metrics upload, alert list, incident summary, owner confirmed.
- Experiment launch checklist: baseline capture, safety gates set, canary traffic definition, rollback plan recorded.
- Graduation checklist: runbook written, dashboard shared, PRs merged, communication plan executed.

End of doc.

Draft history: created 2026-02-10 by Aisha Kapoor; updated 2026-03-02 after pilot labs with notes from Liam and Rosa.
